items.stem: Based on the experiment described in the passage, which of the following is true about the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire?
What is the name of a current-carrying coil that behaves like a magnet?
When current is passed through a cylindrical coil, what happens to the compass needle?
What happens to the strength of an electromagnet if the number of turns in the coil is increased?
Which of the following appliances works on the principle of the heating effect of electric current?
If a student uses a battery with two cells instead of one, what will happen to the heat generated in the wire?
Based on the diagram of the lemon cell, what is the role of the lemon juice in the cell?
Which of the following is an example of the heating effect of electric current?
What is the phenomenon called when a magnetic field is produced around a conductor when electric current flows through it?
What is an electromagnet?
If a nichrome wire is used in an electric heater, which of the following properties makes it suitable for this purpose?
What happens to the magnetic effect of a coil when the current is stopped?
What determines the strength of an electromagnet?
In a circuit with a coil and a compass, what would happen if the coil is made of a non-magnetic material like nichrome and current flows through it?
In the experiment with the magnetic compass and the wire, what happens to the compass needle when the electric current flows through the wire?
Which effect of electric current is used in an electric iron?
What is the main reason rechargeable batteries are preferred over non-rechargeable ones?
What happens to the iron paper clips when the electric current stops flowing through the coil in the electromagnet model?
What does the deflection of the compass needle indicate when current flows through the wire in the experiment?
Which of the following is the reason the wire heats up in an electric circuit?
What would happen if the electric current in the electromagnet is increased by using a higher voltage cell?
If an electromagnet is made using a copper coil, what will happen if the current is stopped?
What happens to the polarity of the ends of an electromagnet when the direction of current is reversed?
